_about.purpose: Find which videos, and which passages inside them, talk about each training topic that RepWise's adaptation engine needs (progression, volume, deload, substitution...). It answers the question: does the corpus have enough material to ground each adaptation rule?
_about.used_by: src/ingestion/coverage_report.py, which writes data/corpus/coverage_matrix.csv, coverage_hits.csv and coverage_summary.md. chunker.py then reads coverage_matrix.csv to tag each chunk with its video's topics.
_about.when_applied: On the cleaned and corrected passages (data/corpus/passages/), so the corrected words (deload, push pull legs...) are found. Passages flagged 'sponsor' are skipped.
how_matching_works: Each topic has a list of patterns (regular expressions, case-insensitive).
A passage counts as one hit for a topic if at least one of its patterns appears in it. A passage can count for several topics.
Patterns match anywhere in a word unless they use \b: 'fatigu' catches fatigue, fatigué, fatiguant. This is on purpose, to catch every form of a French word.
A hit means 'this passage mentions the topic and is worth reading'. It does NOT mean the passage supports a training rule: read the hit before linking a rule to it.

regex_cheat_sheet.\\b: word boundary: '\bsplit' catches 'split' but not a word that merely contains it.
regex_cheat_sheet.(?:a|b): a group of choices: 'temps de (?:repos|récupération)' catches both expressions.
regex_cheat_sheet.s?: the letter before is optional: 'douleurs?' catches 'douleur' and 'douleurs'.
regex_cheat_sheet.[rz]: one of these letters: 'augmente[rz]?' catches augmente, augmenter, augmentez.
regex_cheat_sheet.?: an optional space: 'macro ?cycle' catches 'macrocycle' and 'macro cycle'.

fields.label: short readable name, shown in coverage_summary.md.
fields.description: what the topic covers, which part of RepWise it feeds, and the known noise of its patterns.
fields.patterns: the expressions that make a passage count as a hit.

how_to_tune: Too many irrelevant hits: make a pattern stricter (add \b, require a following word) or remove it.
Missing obvious passages: add the expression Nassim actually uses (check data/corpus/clean_txt/).
After any change, rerun coverage_report.py, then chunker.py, and compare coverage_summary.md.
_about.limits: Keyword matching only: synonyms or ideas expressed without these words are missed, and a word can appear in an unrelated context.

progression.label: Load / rep progression
progression.description: Passages about making training harder over time: progressive overload, adding weight, adding reps or sets. Feeds the load and repetition progression rules. Noise: 'progresser' and 'progression' are also used in a general sense (progressing in life, weight loss progress).

volume.label: Training volume (sets)
volume.description: Passages about how much work is done: number of sets per exercise, per session, per muscle or per week. Feeds the volume adjustment rules (adding or removing sets). Noise: 'volume' can also mean muscle size ('prendre du volume').

effort.label: Effort / proximity to failure
effort.description: Passages about how hard each set is: training to failure, reps in reserve (RIR), perceived exertion (RPE), intensity. Feeds the effort targets and the decision to progress. Note: Nassim talks about 'échec' (failure) and 'intensité', almost never RIR or RPE. 'intensité' and 'à fond' are vague and catch general motivation talk.

rest_intervals.label: Rest between sets
rest_intervals.description: Passages about rest time between sets ('temps de repos', 'récupération entre les séries', 'minutes de repos'). Feeds rest prescriptions and the session duration estimate. Mostly concentrated in one dedicated video.

fatigue_recovery.label: Fatigue, recovery, sleep
fatigue_recovery.description: Passages about fatigue, recovery, sleep, overtraining, soreness and supercompensation. Feeds the recovery checks and the deload triggers. Noise: 'récupérer' is also used for rest between sets and for everyday meanings.

deload.label: Deload / lighter week
deload.description: Passages about deload weeks: a planned lighter week to drop accumulated fatigue ('deload', 'semaine de décharge', 'semaine plus légère'). Feeds the deload rules. Only findable because term_corrections.json fixes the misheard 'dilode'. Coverage is essentially one video.

plateau.label: Plateau / stagnation / regression
plateau.description: Passages about stagnation, plateaus and regression ('stagner', 'plateau', 'régresser', 'ne progresse plus'). Feeds the progression policy switch (what to do after repeated failure). Thin coverage. Noise: 'plateau' can also be a machine platform (leg press).

substitution.label: Exercise substitution / alternatives
substitution.description: Passages about replacing an exercise or using an alternative or variant ('remplacer', 'alternative', 'variante', 'à la place de', 'si vous n'avez pas'). Feeds the exercise substitution map. The exercise ranking videos ('du MEILLEUR au PIRE') are the richest source. Noise: 'au lieu de' and 'à la place de' are common in everyday speech.

cycles.label: Cycles / periodization
cycles.description: Passages about training cycles and periodization: macrocycle, mesocycle, microcycle, phases. Feeds the cycle structure of the program. Noise: '\bcycles?\b' and 'phase de' are broad (a cardio cycle, a fat loss phase).

frequency_split.label: Frequency / split choice
frequency_split.description: Passages about how often to train and how to split the week: full body, split, upper lower, push pull legs, sessions per week. Feeds the initial program structure (frequency and split choice).

break_detraining.label: Missed sessions / breaks / detraining
break_detraining.description: Passages about missed sessions, breaks and detraining: pausing training, losing muscle, coming back without regressing. Feeds the rules for missed sessions and returns after a break. Thin coverage: most of these rules will be implementation assumptions.

pain_safety.label: Pain / injury (safety handling only)
pain_safety.description: Passages that mention pain or injury ('douleur', 'blessure', 'tendinite', 'mal au genou/dos/épaule...'). Used only to route pain reports to safety handling: RepWise never diagnoses or treats injuries, so these passages must not become treatment advice.

beginner.label: Beginner guidance
beginner.description: Passages with advice for beginners ('débutant', 'première année', 'quand on commence'). Feeds experience-appropriate restrictions (red team case RT1: a beginner asking for an advanced routine).

nutrition.label: Nutrition (out of MVP scope)
nutrition.description: Passages about nutrition: calories, protein, deficit, bulking, cutting, carbs. Out of the MVP scope: tracked so these passages can be identified and kept out of training advice, not used to answer.
